chunks: And the evil of what they had earned would become visible to them; and what they used to mock would surround them from all sides.
ai.seo_question: What happens to the evil deeds of disbelievers on the Day of Judgment according to this verse?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the psychological torment of disbelievers as the abstract consequences of their deeds become concrete reality, fulfilling the concept of *haqq* (truth/reality) overtaking them. It underscores the irony that the specific punishment they mocked in the world becomes the inescapable reality that surrounds them, a theme often linked to the transition from *ghaflah* (heedlessness) to *mushahadah* (vision) of divine justice.
